messages:
pagerduty-bot: 🚨 PagerDuty: High - inference-pool-az2 has 20% of pods NotReady (alert: inference-pool-degraded). Triggered at 1956789012
infra-bot: auto-remediation attempted: cordon+drain of node gpu-node-12 failed (kubelet not responding). collecting logs...
jess-oncall: I’m on it. seeing a spike in 5xxs to customers on /v1/generate from this pool. routing policy should have fallback but some long-running streams failed.
sam-ops: log tail from one crashed container:
```
E0720 10:23:45.123456 1 server.cc:456] CUDA: cuCtxCreate failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
```
akash-lead: looks like OOM + kubelet flapping. Are GPU drivers stable on that host?
jess-oncall: nodectl status gpu-node-12:
```
$ kubectl get nodes gpu-node-12 -o wide
NAME         STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-node-12  NotReady   <none>   42d  v1.26.3
```
And kubelet logs show repeated restart loop: "kubelet: panic: runtime error" around the same time.
leo-sre: I’m checking infra metrics: node memory and GPU mem show a jump ~10:23UTC then kubelet heartbeat stopped. no evictions recorded before kubelet died.
pagerduty-bot: Note: 3 customers with high error rates (ids c-101, c-327, c-402). Estimated affected requests: ~1.2k/min.
sam-ops: mitigation plan — 1) remove node from rotation (already cordon failed), 2) scale up alternative pool (dedicated fallback), 3) restart kubelet via cloud provider host action if accessible.
jess-oncall: can we drain pods from the node with --ignore-daemonsets? trying kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --force --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
infra-bot: drain command hung: error waiting for pods: timed out waiting for the condition. kubelet not accepting eviction.
leo-sre: can we bwrap a graceful fallback by promoting warm standby nodes? running scale command now: api: POST /internal/autoscaler/scale with body {"pool":"inference-pool-az2","delta":+6}
akash-lead: yes do it. also please open a support ticket for the host (cloud-provider) to hard-reboot if kubelet won't recover.
jess-oncall: while autoscaler spins up, increment routing weight off az2:
```
$ curl -X POST https://console.internal/routing/adjust -d '{"pool":"inference-pool-az2","weight":0.2}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx'
```
sam-ops: started emergency canary that forces new requests to fallback pool. streaming sessions already open will still fail. need a customer impact blurb.
customer-success-bot: Draft impact note: "We observed degraded inference availability for some customers in region eu-west-1 between 10:23 and ongoing; traffic rerouted. We're actively remediating and will provide ETA." Add affected customer list?
jess-oncall: add c-101 and c-327 as critical. @akash-lead can you approve messaging?
akash-lead: approved. cc @product for postmortem.
infra-bot: cloud-provider support: host is reachable via IP but agent not responding; scheduling reboot (ETA 7m).
leo-sre: autoscaler added 6 nodes, new pods are hitting GPUs and warmup looks ok. latency on fallback pool up ~25ms but error rate dropping.
sam-ops: kubelet on gpu-node-12 just restarted (1956789350). checking pods: some containers crashed on OOM and will be rescheduled.
jess-oncall: reschedule progress: 18/20 pods now recreated on other nodes.
pagerduty-bot: Incident status -> acknowledged by jess-oncall, severity: high. paging suppressed for lower-priority alerts.
leo-sre: after reboot, dmesg shows GPU driver recovering but there are a handful of kernel OOM kills for userland processes prior to kubelet death. suspect memory leak in model runner on that node.
akash-lead: action items: 1) leave node cordoned until we validate driver + runner binary; 2) add node to quarantine group to prevent autoscale reattach; 3) create job to run model-serve binary under profiler on canary host to reproduce leak.
jess-oncall: logging handoff — I need to go offline in 10m. @leo-sre you take next 2hr on-call? I'll post a checklist.
leo-sre: taking handoff. checklist accepted.
jess-oncall: checklist posted:
- confirm affected customers list and notify CSMs
- validate node image + drivers before uncordon
- correlate model runner versions on node with crash times
- add temporary autoscaler rule to keep fallback pool at +4 until root cause fixed
- start postmortem doc and tag incident-1956789012
sam-ops: started postmortem doc: https://wiki.internal/incidents/1956789012 - added initial timeline and logs.
customer-success-bot: CSM notification sent to affected accounts.
leo-sre: observed one remaining flappy pod that enters CrashLoopBackOff — removing from rotation now and marking for deeper debug.
akash-lead: thanks team. keep updates in this thread. I'll join on the postmortem in 30m.
jess-oncall: leaving notes: reboot fixed node but kernel oom saw several model processes >16GB. suspect recent model config change increased batch size. tagging infra-release-2026-07-20 for rollback check. signing off. :wave:
leo-sre: confirmed fallback routing holding, errors down to baseline. will keep monitoring and escalate if SLOs break.
pagerduty-bot: Incident: inference-pool-degraded -> resolved for now (recovery observed), monitoring for 30m.
